objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a breast mass.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I noticed a mass in my right breast about three weeks ago, and it’s been rapidly getting bigger. I haven’t had any pain with it, and I haven’t noticed any changes to the skin or nipple.
Thank you for sharing that. To help narrow this down, I need to ask: **How old are you, and are you currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or have you recently stopped breastfeeding?**
Patient: I’m 45 years old. I’m not pregnant or breastfeeding, and I haven’t recently stopped breastfeeding.
Is the mass mobile when you press on it, or does it feel fixed to your chest wall or skin?
Patient: It feels firm and seems fixed to the area of my chest rather than freely moving around. I haven’t noticed it sliding over the skin when I press on it.
Have you noticed any lumps or swelling in your armpit on the same side?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or swelling in my armpit on that side.
Have you noticed any warmth over the mass, or has the skin appeared red at all, even if it comes and goes?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any warmth over the mass, and I haven’t seen any redness of the skin over it.
Have you had any nipple discharge, especially bloody or clear fluid, from the right breast?
Patient: I haven’t had any nipple discharge from my right breast, including no bloody or clear fluid.
Have you had any personal history of breast cancer or breast biopsies before, and do you have any first-degree relatives (mother, sister, daughter) with breast or ovarian cancer?
Patient: I haven’t had any breast cancer or breast biopsies before, and I don’t have any first-degree relatives with breast or ovarian cancer.
Have you had any recent trauma to the breast, such as a bump or injury, or are you taking any blood thinners?
Patient: I don’t recall any recent trauma or injury to the breast, and I’m not taking any blood thinners.

Approximately how large is the mass now compared to when you first noticed it three weeks ago (for example, has it grown from grape-sized to golf ball-sized), and do you notice any visible asymmetry between your breasts when you look in the mirror?

Patient: It’s grown noticeably in just three weeks—now about the size of a golf ball, and it wasn’t anywhere near that size at the beginning. I also do notice visible asymmetry between my right and left breast when I look in the mirror.
Have you noticed any dimpling or puckering of the skin over the mass, or has your nipple been pulled inward or changed position compared to before?

Doctor: Have you noticed any dimpling or puckering of the skin over the mass, or has your nipple been pulled inward or changed position compared to before? Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any dimpling or puckering of the skin, and my nipple hasn’t been pulled inward or changed position.
Are you currently taking hormone replacement therapy, birth control pills, or any other hormonal medications, and have you gone through menopause yet?
Patient: I’m not taking hormone replacement therapy or birth control pills, and I don’t take any other hormonal medications. I’ve gone through menopause—my last period was a few years ago.
